title: Create Comparison Labels with CASE WHEN
learning_objective: Learn how to turn numeric comparisons into readable labels.

tutorial.explanation: CASE WHEN lets SQL choose a text label based on conditions. This is useful when you need to say whether one value is higher, lower, or the same as another value.
tutorial.syntax: CASE WHEN salary > 80000 THEN 'higher' WHEN salary < 80000 THEN 'lower' ELSE 'same' END AS salary_label
tutorial.mental_model: CASE checks conditions from top to bottom. The first true condition wins. ELSE handles anything that did not match.

guided_example.prompt: Label each employee's salary as higher, lower, or same compared with 80000.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT employee_name, salary, CASE WHEN salary > 80000 THEN 'higher' WHEN salary < 80000 THEN 'lower' ELSE 'same' END AS salary_label FROM employees;
guided_example.explanation: The CASE expression compares each row's salary to 80000 and returns a label for that row.

practice.prompt: Return employee_name and comparison_result, where comparison_result compares salary to 80000 using 'higher', 'lower', or 'same'.
practice.expected_query: SELECT employee_name, CASE WHEN salary > 80000 THEN 'higher' WHEN salary < 80000 THEN 'lower' ELSE 'same' END AS comparison_result FROM employees;

hints: CASE WHEN belongs in the SELECT list.
Use ELSE 'same' for the equal case.
